data.description:
## Context / Problem

`rebar create` today warns only when a new title normalizes byte-identically to a recent one: `duplicate_create_warning` (`src/rebar/_commands/recent_creates.py:117`), gated by `verify.suggest_duplicate_tickets` (`:129`), matching on `title_norm` equality (`:103`). ADR 0122 measured that stratum at 1,431 of 1,524 recorded duplicate pairs. The remaining 93 pairs differ in wording and are invisible to equality matching; they are why agents re-file work that already has a ticket.

This story builds the whole user-visible feature on a retrieval tier that needs no model provider, no credentials and no network, and is therefore available in every installation. The parent's embedding tier is a later, opt-in ranking upgrade over the same index, catch-up and surfacing machinery this story delivers.

## Approach

**Retrieval.** sqlite FTS5 over title and description with bm25 weights title 5.0 / description 1.0 — the exact configuration ADR 0122 measured as the `fts5` baseline (`evals/similar-tickets/measure.py:389-396`, weights `"0.0, 5.0, 1.0"`). It reaches semantic recall@5 0.823 against the adopted `vector` candidate's 0.876, and is distinguishably better at lexical recall@10 (0.993 vs 0.972, p=0.0000), which ADR 0122 records as the reason it is not removed. Query is the new ticket's title plus the first 200 characters of its description, per ADR 0122's architecture section.

**Top 5, not another count.** ADR 0122's decision is scoped to k=5: at k=10 `vector`'s semantic edge is indistinguishable (p=0.3438) while `fts5`'s lexical edge becomes significant, an operating point at which the evidence favours building nothing. Surfacing a different count invalidates the ADR's comparison and would require re-running `measure.py --paired`.

**Persistence.** A sqlite file under `.rebar/cache/similar-tickets/`, mirroring the git-ignored derived cache `.rebar/cache/plan-review/` already uses (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/checkpoints.py:33-37`). `.gitignore:23` ignores `.rebar/*` wholesale, so no ignore change is needed and nothing derived can reach the `tickets` branch by construction.

**Freshness.** The existing `compute_dir_hash(ticket_dir, event_filenames)` (`src/rebar/reducer/_cache.py:122`), which hashes the reducer version plus each event file's name, size and nanosecond mtime. Reusing it means no new freshness mechanism: one stat per file already detects additions, deletions and same-size rewrites.

**Catch-up is synchronous and read-phase.** Before serving a query, the index reconciles any tickets whose dir hash has changed since it was last built, then answers. There is no daemon, no background thread and no CI trigger, so the feature behaves identically on a fresh clone, under MCP, and in an environment with no CI provider at all. A cold first create pays the full build; the parent's 500 ms bound is scoped to a warm index, and this story records the measured cold figure rather than bounding it.

**Surfacing reuses the advisory seam rather than adding one.** `duplicate_warning` and `description_warning` already ride the create result across all three surfaces: library and MCP as a result key (`src/rebar/types.py:276`, `src/rebar/_lib_writes.py:179`), CLI on stderr so stdout stays pure in both output modes (`src/rebar/_commands/composer.py:463-467`, whose comment states the rationale — the create already succeeded, so the advisory is advisory and the exit code stays 0). `src/rebar/schemas/create_result.schema.json` already documents that contract. Adding `similar_tickets` to the same result inherits three-surface parity instead of rebuilding it.

**Never blocks a create.** The advisory is computed after the write succeeds and every failure path yields an empty field, following the bare `except Exception` at `recent_creates.py:150` that already makes the duplicate advisory incapable of failing a completed write.

The gate is `verify.suggest_duplicate_tickets`, the key that already gates create-time duplicate advice; this is the same advice, better ranked, so a second key would split one user-facing behaviour across two switches. The mechanism-delta ratchet is satisfied by adding no new config key; if the implementation nonetheless introduces a ratcheted mechanism, it carries a `# mechanism-ok:` marker at the definition site naming this ticket.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A `similar_tickets` advisory carrying at most 5 entries of (id, alias, title, score) is returned by `rebar create --output json`, by the library `create_ticket` return dict, and by MCP `create_ticket`, and is described in `create_result.schema.json`. Checked by: one parity test per surface asserting the field's presence and shape on the same created ticket.
- [ ] With no model provider configured and every provider credential environment variable unset, a create against a seeded store returns a non-empty ranked `similar_tickets` advisory. Checked by: an integration test that clears the credential environment and asserts the advisory is non-empty.
- [ ] Against a synthetic store the test itself generates and asserts to hold at least 10,000 tickets, create-time retrieval with a warm index completes within a p95 of 500 ms over at least 20 runs. Checked by: a timing test that asserts the generated store's ticket count before measuring.
- [ ] After 100 creates and 100 reads against a test store, the `tickets` branch contains only user event types and no derived search data. Checked by: an integration test asserting the branch's event-type set after the run.
- [ ] A ticket created on a clone is returned as a candidate by the next create on that same clone, in one process, with no daemon, MCP server, background thread or CI involved. Checked by: an integration test performing both creates in-process. The measured cold catch-up p95 for that store is recorded as a comment on this ticket.
- [ ] A create succeeds with exit status 0 and an empty `similar_tickets` advisory when the index file is absent, when it is corrupt, and when catch-up raises. Checked by: one test per failure mode asserting both the exit status and the advisory contents.
- [ ] Every module added or modified under `src/rebar/` is at most 800 lines, and `python scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py --check` and `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` both exit 0. Checked by: running the two scripts and `make verify`.
data.title: Surface similar tickets at create time on a provider-free lexical index
